title: Printing a variable
summary: Join text and values with + so the output says what it means.

say.never: Put a `+` between some text and a variable and Java **joins** them into one piece of text. That's how you add a label to a number, so the output says what it means. For example `"Team number: " + teamNumber` prints `Team number: 4143`.
say.bit: `+` between a String and a value **joins** them into one String. That's how you label what you print.

marks.label: joins the text and the value

say.never: The checker reads exactly what your program prints, so it must match perfectly: the same capital letters, the colon, and the single space. Look at the three examples on the board: only the first one is exactly right.
say.bit: The checkpoints read your output, so it must match exactly: capital letters, the colon, the one space.

board.code:
System.out.println("Team number: " + teamNumber);  // Team number: 4143
System.out.println("Team number:" + teamNumber);   // Team number:4143
System.out.println("team number: " + teamNumber);  // team number: 4143
